clue.text: Cook makes tarts for a demanding employer

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or falsify it, so the following letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A harsh boss treats the bakery's pastries as a mere excuse to make staff work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person in the kitchen, but it is the anagram signal working on MAKES TARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss who sets heavy work and drives staff hard is a stern overseer of labour.

clue.text: One produces low music, giving rise to an objection

indicators.note: in a down clue giving rise means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A musician produces low notes that provoke complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving rise to' looks like causing, but in a down clue it reverses A BUT upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brass instrument plays in the bass register.

clue.text: Sullage could be bad for this bird

indicators.note: could be bad suggests the letters of the waste word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Dirty water could harm the seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: Sullage is sewage or filthy water.
explanation.definitionFit: A common coastal bird with a raucous call, found around harbours.

clue.text: Lucrative venture — device to make bread roll?

definitions.meaning: a business that brings in lots of profit
bread is slang for money and roll means spin, so a gadget that sets cash whirling

explanation.surface: A profitable enterprise, or a kitchen gadget for bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread roll' tempts a baking reading; split it as bread (money) plus roll (spin).
explanation.definitionFit: A profitable business earns plenty of cash; and literally a thing that sets cash revolving.

clue.text: Nothing new in tinker being slipshod

indicators.note: in means the nothing and new pieces are placed inside the tinker's letters

parts.note: a tinker in the old sense is a mischievous rogue, and so sly or crafty
love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A careless repairman has no new parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' suggests a mender of pots, but is read in its old sense of a mischievous rogue; 'in' places the nothing and new pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless and untidy in habits or work, like a sloppy craftsman.

clue.text: Free from former futile cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: cut means the word for futile is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: empty means futile or hollow, as in empty threats

explanation.surface: Liberated from a past that was pointless and cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' removes the final Y of EMPTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Released from an obligation or duty that others must meet.

clue.text: Broadcast supporting member

definitions.meaning: to transmit a signal or programme by radio
a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.surface: A radio report about a structural component.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a signal is to send it out; a structural girder is a load-bearing piece of a building.

clue.text: Issue English volunteers raised after call-up

indicators.note: after means the volunteers come later than the call
in a down clue up means the call word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: raised means the English and volunteers letters are lifted, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: English reservists are summoned to service once conscription begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call-up' looks like conscription, but splits: 'up' turns the call word upward, and 'raised' turns E plus TA into ATE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow out or proceed from a source is to come forth.

clue.text: Anthology produced by fellow unknown outside one's small group

indicators.note: outside means the fellow and unknown pieces go round the others

parts.note: man means a fellow or chap
one's reads as I'S, with I for one
a cell is a small group, as in a terrorist or party cell
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A collection is compiled by a stranger from outside a small circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' puts the fellow-plus-unknown pair round the rest, splitting as M ... ANY; 'small group' is a cell in the political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of assorted pieces of writing gathered in one volume.

clue.text: Mental ability of supporter holding political office

parts.note: a bra is a garment that supports, a common crossword trick
a party holding office is said to be in power

explanation.surface: A question about how clever someone must be to stand behind a politician in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a political backer, but it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence or capacity for thought is the force of a person's intellect.

clue.text: Northern girl requires Southern girl's backing

indicators.note: backing means the letters for southern and the girl's name are read from the end to the start

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south or southern
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A girl from the north depends on support from a girl in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it turns the pieces round: S plus SAL becomes LASS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a young woman is used chiefly in northern England and Scotland.

clue.text: Get a move on and suppress the idle chatter

parts.note: to step on something is to crush or suppress it
taken as written
gas is idle talk, as in a good gas

explanation.surface: Hurry up and stop the pointless gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'gas' can mean empty talk; the answer means press the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry up is literally to press the accelerator pedal of a car.

clue.text: Avenging spirit's violent passion

definitions.meaning: one of the Furies, the avenging goddesses of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A vengeful ghost driven by uncontrollable anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erinyes of myth are the avenging goddesses; and wild rage is an extreme anger.

clue.text: Speak at length, but make amends for taking a time

indicators.note: taking means one piece takes in, or contains, the other pieces

parts.note: to expiate is to atone or make amends for a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to apologise goes on and on about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' puts A and T inside EXPIATE, giving EXP-AT-IATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound or enlarge on a subject is to talk about it in great detail.

clue.text: Obstruct plot, being a peevish type

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart or obstruct them
a patch is a plot of ground

explanation.surface: Blocking someone's scheme makes them grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, irritable person is a grouch.

clue.text: Podgy fellow introducing learner to old college

indicators.note: introducing means the fellow's name has the learner letter brought into it

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
L is the learner sign on British practice cars
a poly, short for polytechnic, was a type of British college before 1992

explanation.surface: A plump man enrols a learner at a former polytechnic.
explanation.walkthrough: British polytechnics became universities in 1992, so POLY is an old college.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and round in shape, as of a chubby child.

clue.text: Request a former PM to speak

indicators.note: to speak signals that the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s, so a former PM gives A PEEL

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an old Prime Minister to address them.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest plea or petition is a request.

clue.text: Food commonly served behind bars

parts.note: reads as prison meals, but also the British slang for time spent in jail, served as a sentence

explanation.surface: What prisoners typically eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'doing' this oat dish means serving a prison term, so 'served' does double duty in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal boiled in milk or water is a breakfast food, and British slang for a jail sentence.

clue.text: Keeping a low profile, back down

definitions.meaning: lying with one's back downwards, face up

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of sight and gives way in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back down' reads as retreat in an argument, but here it means lying on one's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat on one's back, face upward, is the sense of both readings.

clue.text: University in London area is widely approved

indicators.note: in means the university letter is set inside the London district

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A university in a part of London has a good reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Liked or admired by many people is the sense of being well received.

clue.text: Departing relative's suspect behaviour

parts.note: going means leaving or departing
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family member is leaving under a cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious or improper activities are what people whisper about as shady happenings.

clue.text: She's married abroad, so a ring must be taken out

indicators.note: taken out suggests the letters are taken apart and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A married woman overseas must remove her wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's married abroad' defines an Italian title for a married woman, Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a married woman, equivalent to Madam or Mrs.

clue.text: Grieve for bird no longer living in part of the Highlands

indicators.note: in means the extinct bird is placed inside the Scottish word

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: Someone mourns an extinct bird that once lived in the Scottish mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament or mourn over a loss is to express sorrow about it.

clue.text: A manipulative type, with strings attached, possibly

definitions.text: A manipulative type, with strings attached, possibly

parts.words: A manipulative type, with strings attached, possibly
parts.note: reads as a scheming person who attaches conditions, but describes someone working marionettes on strings

explanation.surface: A scheming person whose favours always come with conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who works marionettes controls them by strings, and figuratively controls others behind the scenes.

clue.text: Intoxicated, but able to win a trick

definitions.meaning: drunk or under the influence of drugs
in card games a top-ranking card beats lower ones

explanation.surface: A drunk card player still takes a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drunk or drugged is being elevated in slang; a top card ranks above the rest.

clue.text: How trucks deliver goods for mass producer

definitions.meaning: ..., short for by road, the way lorries carry freight
William ..., the Tudor composer who wrote settings of the Mass

explanation.surface: Lorries delivering for a factory turning out goods in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass producer' suggests a factory, but means a composer of Masses: William Byrd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan church composer wrote three famous Latin Mass settings.

clue.text: Coral reef's no longer a ring

indicators.note: no longer means the following letter is now absent from the reef word

parts.note: an atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef

explanation.surface: A coral reef no longer forms a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like the shape of the reef, but it is the definition: to sound a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound a bell slowly, as for a funeral, is to peal it.

clue.text: Smugly virtuous pair of old women

indicators.note: pair of means the word for an old woman is used twice

parts.note: Goody, short for goodwife, was an old title for a woman of humble rank

explanation.surface: Two elderly ladies are prim and self-righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatiously well-behaved and self-satisfied about one's own good conduct.

clue.text: Rather dreary setting for such ordinary people

indicators.note: setting for means the words form a mount that holds the letters within them

explanation.surface: A dull backdrop is what common folk are given.
explanation.definitionFit: The common mass of people, thought of as following one another like cattle.

clue.text: Get it where market trader may keep spare stock

definitions.text: where market trader may keep spare stock
definitions.meaning: beneath the stall, read as two words

explanation.surface: A stallholder explains where the extra goods are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a meaning is to comprehend it; extra goods are stowed beneath the stall.
